editorial:
In 1930s Korea under Japanese rule, a young pickpocket named Sook-hee gets a job as a handmaiden to a rich heiress named Hideko. Her real job is to help a fake Count trick Hideko into marriage so they can steal her money. But the plan gets messy when feelings and secrets start changing everything. The movie mixes romance, danger, and twists in a beautiful old estate, and you never quite know who is telling the truth.

The acting is really strong, the costumes and sets are very gorgeous, and the story keeps surprising you with new angles. It can be slow at times and has some intense adult scenes, so it is not for everyone. If you enjoy clever thrillers with romance and betrayal, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the end, Hideko and Sook-hee turn the tables on both the fake Count and Uncle Kouzuki. The Count is trapped and killed, while Kouzuki is left behind as the women escape together with the fortune. The final scenes show them leaving for a new life, free from the men who tried to control them. The twist is that the maid and heiress were never truly enemies.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever thrillers with romance and betrayal.
